newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Jan-May world air cargo up 4.1pct, reports ACI.
newsitem.headline: Jan-May world air cargo up 4.1pct, reports ACI.

text.p: Freight and mail traffic handled by 460 airports around the world between January and May 1996, totalled 19.43 million tonnes, up 4.1 percent on the same period the previous year, said Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI).
North America, the biggest of ACI's six cargo-handling regions, reported 10.23 million tonnes of freight traffic, up 3.9 percent on January-May 1995.

Airports in the Asia/Pacific region (in which ACI incorporates Indo-China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Malaysia and Australia), tabled cargo throughput of 3.97 million tonnes, an increase of 4.2 percent on the first five months of last year, ACI said.
ACI's European member airports handled tonnage totalling 4.05 million tonnes, a rise of 4.2 percent on the same period in 1995.
Middle Eastern airports recorded the highest growth rate of ACI's cargo-handling regions in the months in question, with throughput rising 18.8 percent to 689,571 tonnes.
By contrast, Latin America and Caribbean airports, saw January-May 1996 freight traffic handled down 10.9 percent on 1995 levels at 419,819 tonnes.
African airports cargo traffic showed a 3.1 percent growth to 72,888 tonnes. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel:+44 171 542 7706 Fax:+44 171 542 5017
